overview: Welfare Mechanism: 110 official Qs (2008-2025), mostly one-liners (92) plus 9 negative, 6 statement-based and 3 matching/odd-pair/multiple-correct. Public policies and welfare programmes dominate (45 Qs, with 21 in 2019 alone), then Women (17), Children (13) and STs (11). APPSC asks who/what a scheme targets, its year, its amount, which ministry runs it and which Article, Schedule or authority applies to a group. AP state schemes are a regular share.

possibility.angle: Wage-employment and anti-poverty programmes (FFW, NREP, RLEGP, JRY, MGNREGA; self-employment IRDP, PMRY, DDU-GKY, PM Vishwakarma)
possibility.what_they_ask: Year of start or enactment, unit and days of the MGNREGA entitlement, wage vs self-employment class, implementing agency, target group, loan amount

possibility.angle: Central flagship schemes and missions (Ujjwala, PMSBY, SBM-G, SPMRM, JJM, SAGY, Bharat Nirman, RSBY, PMKSY, DBT, Aspirational Districts, Twenty-Point Programme)
possibility.what_they_ask: Aim or beneficiary, launch date, target date, Centre-State fund ratio, who chairs a committee, which components a scheme has, premium amount

possibility.angle: AP state welfare schemes and bodies (Indiramma, Deepam, NTR Sujala, NTR Nagar, Pedarikampai Gelupu, Vidya Deevena, Chedodu, Thodu, SERP, APMSS, AP poverty data)
possibility.evidence: 10 Qs in leaf /1 (2008×2, 2017×4, 2019×3, 2024), and more AP items under the BC, Women, Minorities and Children angles
possibility.what_they_ask: Scheme to beneficiary group, amount per beneficiary, acronym expansion, number of beneficiaries or houses, which body runs it

possibility.angle: Welfare ministries, councils, acts and policy milestones (MoSJE renaming, senior-citizen council, CAPART, ESI ceiling, food laws, NPE, Year of Social Justice)
possibility.what_they_ask: Parent ministry, full name after renaming, year of an Act, wage ceiling, purpose of a body

possibility.angle: Provisions for Scheduled Castes (Art 334 extensions, 82nd Amendment, PoA Act case law, manual scavenging, SC schemes)
possibility.what_they_ask: Amendment number for a change, Supreme Court case name, activist or organisation, technology used, incentive amount

possibility.angle: Provisions for Scheduled Tribes (Fifth and Sixth Schedules, TAC, Art 164 tribal minister, NCST, GCC; PESA from related exams)
possibility.evidence: 11 Qs: 2017×7, 2019×2, 2024, 2025; PESA asked often in other APPSC exams
possibility.what_they_ask: Who declares or alters areas vs who makes regulations, member limits, which States, which Schedule applies where, AP tribal institutions

possibility.angle: Provisions for Minorities (Art 30, 350A, NCM, Sachar, AP Dulhan)
possibility.what_they_ask: Committee chair and its classification, Article number, who appoints NCM, whether the rights are absolute, scheme amount

possibility.angle: Provisions for BCs (Art 340, Mandal and Kalelkar, OBC quota cases, AP BC schemes)
possibility.what_they_ask: Commission chair and year, government that appointed it, petitioner in a case, whether 'backward class' is defined, AP scheme target

possibility.angle: Provisions for Women (NCW, maternity law, POSH, Dowry Act, RMK, DWCRA, PMMVY, Ujjwala, women in legislatures, AP SHG schemes)
possibility.what_they_ask: Year or date in force, leave weeks, full form, which bank or body, the person behind a quote, representation percentages, AP SHG scheme aims

possibility.angle: Provisions for the Disabled (National Trust, RCI Act, RPwD, disability sports, MoUs)
possibility.what_they_ask: What an Act or initiative provides, which disability group, location of a new centre, partner country

possibility.angle: Provisions for Children (RTE, ICDS, Mission Vatsalya, PM CARES for Children, creche, mid-day meal, Amma Vodi)
possibility.what_they_ask: Funding share, grass-root functionary, which ministries converge, age bands and amounts, training body, scheme name for a stated aim

traps.trap: [Unit swap] MGNREGA unit and days swapped: individual vs household, 100 vs 150
traps.spot: Four options that pair 'adult' or 'household' with 100 or 150 days
traps.fix: The entitlement is 100 days per rural household per financial year. 150 days applies only in notified drought or calamity areas and to FRA-patta ST households.
traps.pyq: '100 days to every household … whose adult members volunteer' → household, 100 [prelims-2017#117]

traps.trap: Self-employment scheme hidden in a list of wage-employment schemes (or the reverse)
traps.spot: 'Which is not a wage employment / direct-attack programme'
traps.fix: Wage: FFW, NREP, RLEGP, JRY, SGRY, MGNREGS. Self: IRDP, TRYSEM, PMRY, SGSY, PMEGP. Family planning is neither.
traps.pyq: PMRY among MGNREGS/RLEGP/NREP → PMRY is self-employment [mains-2017-paper3#16]; Family Planning is not a direct attack on poverty [group2-2008-paper3#45]

traps.trap: President and Governor roles swapped in the Fifth and Sixth Schedules
traps.spot: 'Who declares / alters / makes regulations / organises autonomous districts'
traps.fix: Fifth Schedule: the President declares or alters Scheduled Areas, and the Governor makes regulations and can bar or modify laws. Sixth Schedule: the Governor organises and reorganises autonomous districts.
traps.pyq: Alter boundary → President [prelims-2017#69]; regulations → Governor [prelims-2017#68]; 'Only the President can organise autonomous districts' is false [mains-2025-paper1#149]

traps.trap: Statutory bodies dressed up as constitutional ones (and who appoints)
traps.spot: Commission chair or appointment questions on NCM, NCW, NCSC, NCST
traps.fix: NCSC (338), NCST (338A) and NCBC (338B) are constitutional and appointed by the President. NCM (1992 Act) and NCW (1990 Act) are statutory, and their members are nominated by the Union Government.
traps.pyq: Who appoints NCM members → Union Government [mains-2019-paper2#130]

traps.fix: 79th (1999) took SC/ST seat reservation to 2010. 82nd (2000) added the Art 335 proviso on relaxed marks. 350A covers the mother tongue at primary stage, 351 covers Hindi and 300A covers property.
traps.pyq: Extension to 2010 → 79 [group2-2008-paper2#87]; relaxation of qualifying marks in promotion → 82nd [prelims-2024#83]; mother-tongue instruction → 350A [prelims-2017#75]

traps.trap: Scheme paired with a neighbouring scheme's target group
traps.spot: Odd-pair or 'aim of' questions on look-alike names
traps.fix: Fix each scheme to one beneficiary: Vishwakarma for artisans, Navodayam for MSME loan restructuring, Thodu for street vendors and Ujjwala for LPG to BPL women.
traps.pyq: 'YSR Navodayam … transport sector' is the wrong pair [prelims-2024#107]; 'PM Vishwakarma … fishermen' is false [prelims-2024#111]

traps.trap: Ages, dates and amounts shifted inside a true-sounding statement
traps.spot: Statement-based Qs with ages, rupee limits or launch dates
traps.fix: PM CARES for Children was announced 29 May 2021, gives a stipend from 18 and Rs 10 lakh at 23. PM Vishwakarma loans are Rs 1 lakh + Rs 2 lakh (3 lakh total), not 6 lakh.
traps.pyq: 'launched 11 March 2020 … stipend from 14' are both false → I and II [prelims-2024#81]

traps.trap: 'Sole' or 'fully' funding when the scheme is cost-shared
traps.spot: Options such as 'Central government has the sole responsibility' or 'fully funded by'
traps.fix: RTE financing is concurrent (Centre + States). ICDS is a CSS at 60:40 (90:10 NE/Himalayan). Rurban is 60:40.
traps.pyq: RTE 'central government has the sole responsibility for … funds' is not a feature [mains-2017-paper3#42]; ICDS → shared funding [prelims-2017#110]

traps.trap: Commission chair or case name swapped across BC milestones
traps.spot: Chair or petitioner names: Kalelkar/Mandal, Indra Sawhney/Ashoka Kumar Thakur
traps.fix: First BC Commission: Kalelkar (1953-55). Second: B.P. Mandal (1979-80, Janata govt). OBC jobs case: Indra Sawhney (1992). OBC education quota: Ashoka Kumar Thakur (2007-08).
traps.pyq: 2007 stay on 27% OBC education quota → Ashoka Kumar Thakur [group2-2008-paper2#83]; Second BC Commission → B.P. Mandal [group2-2008-paper2#78]

traps.trap: Wrong State slipped into the Art 164(1) tribal-minister list
traps.spot: Multiple-correct State list with Punjab or UP
traps.fix: Since the 94th Amendment (2006) the list is Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP and Odisha. Bihar was dropped.
traps.pyq: MP, Jharkhand, Odisha → I, IV and V [prelims-2024#89]

techniques.name: [Who gets what] Beneficiary-mechanism match
techniques.how: For any scheme, first ask who gets it (group) and what they get (cash, loan, asset, skill or service). Drop options whose group or mechanism cannot fit the name.
techniques.example: DDU-GKY = Grameen Kaushalya, so rural skilling: 'differently abled', 'dry land farmers' and 'artisans' fall → Rural youth [mains-2017-paper3#70]; Adarana (tools to artisans) vs Pelli Kanuka (marriage) vs Pasupu Kumkuma (SHGs) → Adarana [prelims-2019#139]

techniques.name: Programme-timeline ladder
techniques.how: Keep the chain FFW 1977 → NREP 1980 → RLEGP 1983 → JRY 1989 → SGRY 2001 → NFFWP 2004 → NREGA 2005/06 and place the asked item on it. Separate 'enacted' from 'launched'.
techniques.example: 'Food for work started' with 1962/1971/1977/1984 → Janata-era 1977 [mains-2017-paper3#73]; NREGA 'enacted' → 2005, not the 2006 launch [prelims-2019#103]

techniques.name: Schedule-paragraph role map
techniques.how: Draw two columns: Fifth Schedule (Scheduled Areas, any State; TAC ≤20; President declares; Governor regulates) and Sixth Schedule (only Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; district and regional councils; Governor organises). Test every statement against the column.
techniques.example: Sixth Schedule statements: 'all States with >40% ST' is false (4 States), 'outside State executive' is false, 'only the President organises' is false, 'no High Court jurisdiction' is false → None [mains-2025-paper1#149]; autonomous region = unit within a district [prelims-2017#70]

techniques.name: Kill one statement, then read the options
techniques.how: In statement-based Qs, find the statement you can test with one number or date. Strike every option that contains it (or lacks it). Often one option is left.
techniques.example: AP 2019 Assembly women '11.74%' is false (14 of 175, about 8%). Options with III fall, leaving only 'I, II and IV' [prelims-2024#78]

techniques.name: Acronym and name expansion
techniques.how: Expand the acronym word by word. The 'named after a person' option and options outside the expanded field are lures.
techniques.example: INDIRAMMA = Integrated Novel Development in Rural Areas and Model Municipal Areas, so the 'named after Indira Gandhi' option is a lure [group2-2008-paper3#97]; CAPART (People's Action + Rural Technology) → Rural development [prelims-2017#124]

techniques.name: Date-the-scheme for 'not part of' questions
techniques.how: For 'not a flagship of X' or 'not a component of Y', date each item or recall the programme's fixed component list. The item from another era or another field is the answer.
techniques.example: Antyodaya Anna Yojana dates from 2000, so it is not a Modi flagship [mains-2019-paper1#48]; Bharat Nirman's six infrastructure parts exclude NRLM [mains-2019-paper1#107]

techniques.name: Lock the unique year in Act-year matching
techniques.how: Fix the pair you are surest of (the newest or oldest Act), then the next one. Read the options only after two locks.
techniques.example: FSSA is the 2006 one (IV-B) and Grading and Marking is the 1937 one (II-D). PFA 1954 and ECA 1955 follow → I-C, II-D, III-A, IV-B [mains-2019-paper2#82]

confusions.remember: Fifth = Scheduled Areas in any State, TAC; Sixth = 4 NE States (AMTM), autonomous district councils
President draws or redraws the map; Governor governs inside it (regulations, laws not to apply)
TAC ≤20, about 3/4 ST MLAs; ADC ≤30 (up to 4 nominated)
338/338A/338B constitutional, appointed by the President; NCM 1992 and NCW 1990 statutory, nominated by the Centre
First BC Commission 1953-55; Second 1979-80 (Janata appoints, V.P. Singh's Janata Dal implements 1990)
OBC quota in jobs, 50% cap and creamy layer vs OBC quota in central education institutions
Sachar = Muslim socio-economic status (Ashraf/Ajlaf/Arzal); Misra = religious and linguistic minorities
Ajlaf ~ OBC-like; Arzal ~ SC-like; Ashraf ~ upper
Wage = work on public assets for wages; self = credit + subsidy for own unit
Suraksha = accident, Rs 12 (Rs 20 from 2022); Jeevan Jyoti = life, Rs 330 (Rs 436 from 2022)
Ujjwala = LPG to poor women (MoPNG 2016); UJALA = LED bulbs; Saubhagya = household electricity
350A mother-tongue instruction at primary stage; 350B Special Officer for linguistic minorities
340 BC commission; 341 SC list; 342 ST list
SERP = rural poverty (2000, Velugu/IKP); MEPMA = urban poverty
AWW = WCD's ICDS centre; ASHA and ANM = health ministry's NHM
Shakti = women safety and empowerment (incl. Palna creche); Vatsalya = child protection
RMK = micro-credit to women via NGOs; DWCRA = IRDP sub-scheme for rural women's groups, merged into SGSY 1999
Vidya = fee reimbursement; Vasathi = hostel and food maintenance (separated 2020)

anchors: MGNREGA: enacted 2005, launched 2 Feb 2006, renamed 2009; 100 days per household; s.17 social audit by Gram Sabha
Wage line: FFW 1977 → NREP 1980 → RLEGP 1983 → JRY 1989 → SGRY 2001 → NREGA 2005/06; self-employment line: IRDP 1978/80 → SGSY 1999 → NRLM 2011
Fifth Schedule: TAC ≤20 members; President declares or alters areas; Governor regulates (incl. land transfer)
Sixth Schedule States: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram
Art 164(1) tribal welfare minister: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP, Odisha (Bihar dropped, 94th Amendment 2006)
82nd Amendment (2000): Art 335 proviso, relaxed marks and standards for SC/ST promotions
Art 340 BC commission; 350A mother tongue; 338/338A/338B NCSC/NCST/NCBC
Second BC Commission: B.P. Mandal, appointed 1 Jan 1979 (Janata), report 31 Dec 1980
Sachar Committee: set up 2005, report Nov 2006
Maternity Benefit Amendment 2017: 26 weeks (fewer than 2 children), 12 weeks otherwise
POSH Act 2013 ← Vishaka 1997; Dowry Prohibition Act in force 1 July 1961
ICDS 1975: CSS 60:40 (90:10 NE/Himalayan); Anganwadi worker is the grass-root functionary
RTE Act 2009: ages 6-14; Centre and States share funding; neighbourhood school within 3 years
SBM-G target 2 Oct 2019; Jal Jeevan Mission (2019) tap water by 2024; SPMRM launched 21 Feb 2016
ESI wage ceiling Rs 21,000 from 1 Jan 2017; PMSBY Rs 12 / PMJJBY Rs 330 (2015 rates)
Ministry of Welfare renamed Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (1998)
Lok Sabha women: crossed 10% first in 15th LS (2009); 17th LS (2019) highest; 106th Amendment assent 28 Sep 2023
checklist: Which group is it: SC, ST, minority, BC, women, disabled or child? Then which Article, Schedule or body serves that group?
For a scheme: who gets it, what they get (cash, loan, asset, skill, service), which ministry runs it, and when it was launched
Constitutional or statutory body? Who appoints? President or Governor?
Numbers: does the unit (household vs person), age band or amount match the scheme's own rule?
Funding words 'sole' or 'fully': check the cost-sharing ratio
Statement-based: test the one statement you can prove with a number or date, then strike options
AP scheme: fix the government phase (2014-19 NTR/Chandranna, 2019-24 YSR/Jagananna) and its target group
